Good morning 👋

Here's a 10-second habit that will save you from bad trades.

Before you enter, imagine the trade has already lost. 

Then ask: why did it lose?

Maybe the answer is "news was due in 20 minutes." Or "I entered in the middle of the range." Or "I was trading against the higher timeframe."

If you can easily explain why it failed, you probably shouldn't take it.

If you genuinely struggle to find a reason, that's a sign the setup is clean.

Professionals call this a pre-mortem. 

It takes seconds and filters out the trades you'd regret.

Reply ✅ if you'll try it today.

Good morning 👋

Ever been stopped out by a few pips, then watched gold reverse and fly to your target?

That wasn't bad luck. It was a liquidity sweep.

Gold loves to push just beyond obvious highs and lows, exactly where most traders put their stops, before making the real move. 

Those stops are fuel for big players to fill their orders.

How to protect yourself:
→ Don't place your stop right at the obvious high or low. Give it room beyond it.
→ If price sweeps a key level and snaps straight back, that's often the setup, not the danger.
→ Wait for the sweep, then enter on the reclaim.

Once you start seeing sweeps, you'll stop being the liquidity.

Tap 🔥 if a stop hunt has caught you this month.

Good morning 👋

One of the most underused tools in trading.

Trading smaller when you're uncertain.

Most traders treat position size as fixed. They always risk the same amount regardless of how clear the setup is, how volatile the market is or how confident they feel going into the session.

The best traders size dynamically.

High conviction setup on a clean level in favourable conditions? Full size.

Market is choppy, news is due, the level is borderline? Half size. Or a quarter.

Sizing down when uncertain doesn't mean you doubt your strategy. 

It means you understand that not all setups are created equal and you're protecting your account on the ones with less edge.

The goal is to be bigger on your best setups and smaller on your worst ones. 

Not the same size on everything.

This week before every trade ask yourself — how confident am I in this setup on a scale of one to ten? 

Anything below a seven gets reduced size.

Reply with your biggest uncertainty right now as a trader ⬇️
Good session today. 📈

Good morning 👋

One practical rule worth adding to your trading this week.

Don't trade the first 15 minutes of any major session open.

The London open and New York open are the most volatile windows of the day. 

Liquidity is thin. Spreads can be wide. Price often makes sharp moves in one direction before reversing hard in the other.

These moves are designed to clear stop losses before the real direction of the session emerges.

The traders who get caught in these spikes are almost always the ones who were in too early.

Here's the approach.
Mark your levels before the session. 

Set an alarm. Wait 15 minutes after the open. Then look for a setup in the direction the market has chosen.

You'll miss some moves. But the ones you catch will have far more follow through. And you'll stop being the person the spike was designed to hit.

Drop a 🔥 if this is something you've been guilty of.

Good session today. 📈

Good morning 👋

Let's talk about drawdown honestly.

Every trader experiences it. 

A run of losses. 

A week where nothing clicks. 

An account that looks smaller than it did a month ago.

Most traders panic. 

They change their strategy. They increase their size to try to recover faster. 

They abandon the very process that was working before the drawdown started.

This is the worst possible response.

Drawdown is not a sign that your strategy is broken. 

It's a statistical certainty for every strategy that has ever existed. Even the best hedge funds in the world have drawdown periods.

The question is never whether you'll face one. It's whether your process can survive it.

Here's what to do during drawdown.
Reduce your size. Not increase it. 

Protect the account. Keep taking the setups your plan says to take. Don't change the strategy mid-drawdown.

The process that got you into profit before the drawdown is the same process that will get you out of it.

Tap ✅ if you've ever changed strategy during a losing streak and made it worse.

Good session today. 📈

Your criteria were written when you were calm. Trust that version of yourself.

Good morning 👋

One final thought to start the week.

The best traders I know all have one thing in common.

They are genuinely comfortable doing nothing.

Most people come to trading from backgrounds where activity equals progress. You work harder you get more done. You put in more hours you earn more money.

Trading punishes that mindset. In trading, forced activity produces losses not gains.

The best sessions of your life will be the ones where you waited patiently for one clean setup, executed it properly and then walked away.

The worst sessions will be the ones where you sat at the screen for hours taking trade after trade trying to force something to happen.

Practise doing nothing. Seriously. Set a timer for 30 minutes. Watch the chart. Touch nothing. Just observe.

You'll be amazed how much you learn about the market when you're not rushing to trade it.

Good session today. 📈
